title: Structured Dialogue Discourse Parsing
research_question: Can dialogue discourse parsing be improved by globally and jointly learning discourse links and relation labels as a structured labeled multi-root non-projective spanning tree rather than making independent local decisions?
methodology: The authors formulate a dialogue's discourse structure as a labeled directed multi-root non-projective spanning tree, jointly scoring links and their discourse relations with structured encoding and matrix-tree learning and performing structured inference with a modified Chiu-Liu-Edmonds procedure. The model uses pretrained language representations and contextual encoding without explicit hand-crafted speaker or turn-relation features. It is evaluated in-domain and cross-domain on STAC game dialogues and Molweni, derived from Ubuntu IRC technical discussions, using UAS/Link F1 and LAS/Link-and-Relation F1, with reported main results averaged over three runs. Additional analyses examine dialogue length, individual relation types, and robustness when speaker and turn information is removed.

key_findings.finding: The proposed parser reaches LAS 59.6 on STAC and 59.9 on Molweni, improving over the previous best results by 2.3 and 1.5 points respectively.

In cross-domain evaluation, the method obtains LAS 38.0 for STAC-to-Molweni and 31.6 for Molweni-to-STAC, beating the best compared baselines by 5.1 and 4.8 points respectively, although it is not best on cross-domain UAS.
The structured parser's performance degrades less than baseline parsers as dialogues become longer.

The structured method improves correct predictions for relations including QA_pair and Comment on STAC and QA_pair and Clarification Question on Molweni, while low-resource relations remain difficult.
Removing speaker and turn information reduces STAC LAS from 59.6 to 54.4 for the proposed parser, compared with 57.3 to 47.8 for the Struct-Aware baseline.
key_findings.section: 5.5 Additional Analyses - Speaker and Turn Feature Robustness

key_findings.finding: The tree conversion does not retain all multi-parent discourse links: 6% of STAC edges are discarded, and when a node has more than one parent only the latest parent is retained; Molweni requires no such edge removal.

Consequently, the evaluated representation does not directly preserve a response EDU that is jointly attached to multiple antecedent propositions, and the experiments do not separately measure multi-question partial replies, unanswered subquestions, or scoped approval or rejection.

limitations: The tree constraint forces each non-root node to a single retained parent, so genuine multi-parent discourse attachment is lost in the transformed STAC data.
The paper assumes elementary discourse units are already segmented rather than evaluating proposition or EDU segmentation jointly with attachment.
The evaluated units are dialogue EDUs or utterances, not explicitly proposition-level components within a multi-question email message.
Neither STAC nor Molweni is a workplace-email corpus; STAC is game chat and Molweni is based on technical Ubuntu IRC discussions.
The evaluation does not report dedicated measures for unanswered questions, partially answered multi-question turns, or the scope of approval and rejection acts.
Cross-domain UAS results are not uniformly better than older baselines, so the improvement is strongest for joint link-and-relation prediction rather than link prediction alone.
raw_claims: Dialogue discourse parsing predicts both links between discourse units and labels for those links.
The method globally models dialogue structure with a latent tree distribution rather than treating every link independently.
STAC contains multiparty online-game dialogue, whereas Molweni is based on Ubuntu IRC technical discussion.
UAS evaluates link existence, while LAS requires both the link and its relation label to be correct.
The proposed system reports 74.4 UAS and 59.6 LAS on STAC in-domain evaluation.
It reports 83.5 UAS and 59.9 LAS on Molweni in-domain evaluation.
The main table reports averages over three runs.
Six percent of STAC graph edges are removed to obtain the tree-like training structure.
For a node with multiple annotated parents, only the latest parent is kept.
QA_pair is among the relations for which the structured parser improves over the comparison baseline.
The study models dialogue-level attachment but does not evaluate proposition-level completeness of replies to multi-part questions.
